description: Postal-address rendering and validation fixture, shared by both runtimes. An address that renders one way on the desktop and another on the portal is the same defect as not storing it, so both products read this file and must produce these exact strings and problem codes. Expected values follow the per-country format pack (shared/address-formats/), which is the authority on what each country writes and in what order. Label expectations are the English fallback `labelFor` / `label_for` produces: the pack's own token in sentence case. The renderer translates the token instead, via the `address` catalogue, so "pin" appears as "PIN code" on screen.

cases.name: India puts the post town and the code on one line, the state under it, and uppercases the town

12 Hospital Road
Ansari Nagar
KOCHI 682011
Kerala

cases.name: Japan writes the largest unit first and leads with the postal mark
A field the country's format cannot place is refused at entry, not lost quietly
The United Arab Emirates has no postal code at all, and calls its level-1 unit an emirate
Ireland calls its postal code an eircode and does not insist on one
cases.formatted:
St James's Hospital
DUBLIN

cases.name: A postal code that does not match its country's pattern is refused
An unanchored pattern would accept this, so the check anchors both ends
A line whose every field is empty is dropped, literal text and all: no bare SINGAPORE
Separators belonging to a field that is present are kept, and the country uppercases both
Every field a country insists on is named when missing, all at once rather than one per attempt
Kosovo, a user-assigned code, is a full entry rather than a fallback
The country code is the one field every address must have

fhir.description: The field set maps one-to-one onto FHIR R4 Address, except sorting_code, which FHIR has no element for and which therefore travels as an extension rather than being dropped. The address is normalised first, so text is what the country actually renders.
